overview: Pure substances come in two forms — one can't be broken down chemically, the other is made of two or more elements combined.
genZNote: Elements are the alphabet. Compounds are the words.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: A pure substance made of only one type of atom; cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
aspects.valueB: A pure substance formed when two or more elements combine chemically in a FIXED ratio.

aspects.label: Can It Be Separated?
aspects.valueB: Can be broken down into its constituent elements by chemical reactions (not physical means).

aspects.label: Properties vs. Constituents
aspects.valueA: n/a — has its own inherent properties by definition.
aspects.valueB: Properties are typically entirely different from its constituent elements (e.g. NaCl vs. sodium metal and chlorine gas).
